To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
oxidative and nitrosive stress, cellular stress responses, and thiol metabolism are altered in patients with Alzheimer disease.
oxidative and nitrative stress, cellular redox homeostasis, and the cellular stress response are altered in Alzheimer's disease.
nitrosative stress is a key factor in the pathogenesis in AD and that the stress responsive genes HO-1 and Trxr represent important targets for the treatment of the disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of oxidative/nitrosative stress in the development and progression of AD.
the identification of novel molecular targets for the development of therapeutic strategies to prevent and/or treat AD.
the role of oxidative stress, nitrosative stress and the cellular stress response in Alzheimer's disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

nitrosative stress plays a key role in the pathogenesis and progression of AD, and that the stress response genes, such as HSP72, HSP70, HSP60 and HO-1, and TRX, may represent important therapeutic targets for the prevention and treatment of AD.
nitrosative stress and oxidative stress are the main culprits in Alzheimer's disease, but the role of nitric oxide in the pathogenesis is still unclear.
the oxidative and nitrosativestress response is increased in AD and that this may be associated with an increase in the cellular stress response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
oxidative/nitrative stress is increased in the brain and blood of patients with AD.
nitrosative stress is involved in AD pathogenesis, and that the induction of the so called vitagenes, such as HO, HSPs and thioredoxin, could represent an effective therapeutic approach in AD.
nitrosative stress and cellular stress response are increased and thiol home-stasis is impaired in Alzheimer's disease (see Figure 1).
The main takeaway from our work is that
oxidative stress is increased in AD and that the cellular stress response is activated, which may be an adaptive mechanism to counteract oxidative damage.
nitrosative stress and the induction of the vitagenes may represent important targets in AD pathogenesis.
the cellular stress response is activated in AD and that the stress-responsive proteins, such as HO, HSPs, and TRX, represent important targets for therapeutic interventions.
